item.title: ledger: reject currency codes with surrounding whitespace
item.brief: Operator request: the currency code must be exactly three uppercase ASCII letters matching ^[A-Z]{3}$ (ISO 4217). The current ledger trims the currency field before validation, so " EUR" is accepted, which breaks that contract. Change validation so the currency field is checked untrimmed: any whitespace or other character around the code is a malformed code, making ledger print the 1-based input line number to stderr and exit 2. Add a test for a padded code (" EUR" and "EUR ") expecting exit 2 with the line number. Keep `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` passing, and keep the README accurate. Commit on the branch Archon creates, with no co-author or generator line.

item.title: reports: per account and currency totals
item.brief: Operator request (authenticated, local chat): our books now hold more than one currency. Change the `reports` Python tool so it reads the CSV produced by `ledger` on stdin and prints per-account totals per account AND currency. Output header `account,currency,total_cents`, rows sorted by account then currency. CSV from the old ledger (no currency column) must still work and counts as USD. A malformed currency code in the input (must be exactly three uppercase ASCII letters) prints an error to stderr and exits with status 2. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing, add tests for multi-currency totals, sorting, the legacy no-currency input, and the malformed-code exit 2, and update the README to describe the input and output format. Follow the shared contract exactly. Commit the change on the branch Archon creates.

item.title: ledger: optional currency column and currency in CSV output
item.brief: Operator request (authenticated, local chat): our books now hold more than one currency. Change the `ledger` Rust tool so it converts a TSV of transactions on stdin into CSV on stdout with a currency per row. Input lines may carry a fourth column, the ISO 4217 currency code (exactly three uppercase ASCII letters, e.g. EUR); when missing the currency is USD. Output header becomes `date,account,amount_cents,currency` and every row gets the currency. A malformed currency code must print an error naming the input line number to stderr and exit with status 2; other input errors keep exiting with status 1. Keep `cargo test` passing, add tests for the currency column (default USD, valid code, malformed code -> exit 2 with line number), and update the README to describe the input and output format. Follow the shared contract exactly. Commit the change on the branch Archon creates.
